project: Online store customer service: "Where is my order?"
model_choice: Declared per component. When a component's model is omitted, the engine selects the lowest cost model of the required tier from the price table it receives, so the result would change whenever a vendor changes a price.

components.name: Question classification
components.note: Reads every customer message and identifies its subject: order status, exchange or payment. Highest volume in the system and 2.4% of the cost. Caching is declared and will not take effect: the prompt is below this model's minimum cacheable length, and the API returns neither an error nor a warning.

components.name: Order resolution agent
components.note: Handles order status requests: queries the order system, the carrier tracking service and the delivery policy before answering. Receives four times fewer requests than the classification and costs thirty six times more. Its iterations consume 62,000 input tokens per request, against 48,000 in the simple estimate.

components.name: Shipping document reader
components.note: Reads the invoice and the carrier documents and extracts the fields the agent requires. Consolidation is performed by code, not by another model call.

components.name: History compressor
components.note: Summarizes the conversation so that the agent does not reprocess the full history. Its output is read by the agent's next iteration, not by a person, which is why it remains on the lower cost tier.

components.name: Answer quality review
components.note: Reviews a 10% sample of the answers. A reviewer on the same tier as the reviewed component adds no assurance, so it remains on the higher tier despite the low volume.
